title: Model Drift Census and Strategic Substitution Playbook for Regulated Verticals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a repeatable, scored inventory (census) of model drift, substitution risk, and price/latency gaps across core open and licensed models for enterprise/regulatory customers (finance, healthcare, gov). The output will be a prioritized substitution playbook that defines when Redwood should route, recommend, or automatically substitute to compatible variants to preserve SLAs and procurement constraints.

Scope: regional model availability and pricing (NA/EU/APAC), model capability drift (2Q rolling window), substitution compatibility (API/format + quality delta), and procurement friction (private deployment licensing, data residency, certification). Deliverables include a competitor matrix, substitution decision tree, threshold alerts for detection, and a short rollout proposal for the Console to expose substitution settings to customers.

Why now: customers in regulated industries have recently flagged model deprecations and procurement bottlenecks. We need a defensible, operational approach that reduces customer surprise, protects latency/quality SLOs, and informs Dedicated capacity procurement decisions.

High-level approach:
- Phase 1 (Research): inventory model variants across public catalogs + partner vendors; ingest pricing and latency profiles; collect enterprise procurement constraints.
- Phase 2 (Quant): run standardized evals (latency-sensitive prompts and vertical test suites) across candidate models and regions to quantify quality delta and cost-per-thousand-token impact.
- Phase 3 (Policy): define substitution triggers (quality delta thresholds, price delta, latency breach, availability loss) and safe-fallback model lists per vertical.
- Phase 4 (Operationalize): wire alerts into Console, add telemetry hooks for substitution events, and create a canary plan for automatic substitution for low-risk customers.

Primary stakeholders: PMx (lead), Solutions Eng, Runtime, Platform Security, Sales (enterprise AE), Legal (for licensing checks).

acceptance_criteria:
1) Completed model inventory with per-region pricing and latency profiles for 12 candidate models.
2) Quantitative delta table showing quality-cost-latency tradeoffs for at least 3 vertical test suites.
3) Draft substitution decision tree with explicit thresholds and fallback lists.
4) Runbook and Console change request ready for engineering grooming.
5) Exec one-pager summarizing customer impact and recommended immediate mitigations.
success_metrics: Substitution playbook reduces manual AE escalations by 30% in pilot
Alerts surface within 5 minutes of model availability changes
deliverables: Model inventory CSV (region x model x price/latency)
Quality delta matrix and visual heatmap
Console UX request + rollout canary plan
One-pager for GTM and AE enablement
data_sources: Public model manifests (Hugging Face, vendor feeds)
risks: Model quality delta hard to quantify for domain-specific prompts
Licensing clauses prevent automated substitution for some vendors
Regional pricing data incomplete or delayed
False positives in substitution alerts could impact SLA-sensitive customers
